description: Importing a Vertex service account key: the account is added with the default location us-central1.

client.body_text:
--pluxy-corpus-boundary
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="file"; filename="key.json"
Content-Type: application/json

{"type":"service_account","project_id":"corpus-project","private_key_id":"corpus","private_key":"{{private_key}}","client_email":"corpus-1@corpus-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com","token_uri":"{{upstream}}/token"}
--pluxy-corpus-boundary--

exceptions.reason: Different management API by design: the new core keeps a login's account in its credential store, not an auth folder, so the reply names the account (account) where today's core names the saved file (auth-file); status, project_id, email and location are as today's.
The new core answers application/json; today's core's gin handler adds a charset to the reply.
The new core checks the key when it imports it, by fetching an access token at the key's token_uri (the fake upstream here); today's core does not contact Google at import.

headers.Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Authorization, Content-Type, X-Api-Key, X-Goog-Api-Key, Anthropic-Version, Anthropic-Beta
headers.Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS
headers.Access-Control-Expose-Headers: X-CPA-TRACE-ID, X-CPA-VERSION, X-CPA-COMMIT, X-CPA-BUILD-DATE, X-CPA-SUPPORT-PLUGIN, X-CPA-HOME-VERSION, X-CPA-HOME-BUILD-DATE, X-SERVER-VERSION, X-SERVER-BUILD-DATE, Location, Retry-After, ETag, X-Request-Id, OpenAI-Request-Id
